_about: Topic clusters around each pillar (category shortlist). One supporting article per day, taken from the highest-priority pillar (list order) whose next article is 'todo'. Each article answers ONE distinct search intent that the pillar page doesn't, links up to its pillar and across to sibling articles, and must pass scripts/similarity.py (<=30% overlap with any page). Never add 'best free X', 'X for small business' or other variants of a shortlist: they duplicate the pillar. Comparisons (X vs Y) live in data/content_queue.json 'items' and need both tools in the pillar. Order: pillars and their todo articles are sorted by the priority of the next article's target_keyword (data/keywords.json: Google US volume estimate x (1 - difficulty/100)). Each article targets target_keyword in its title, H1, first 100 words and URL slug where natural, and covers close variants and questions people ask.
rules: One keyword, one URL. Every article's target_keyword must be free: run `python3 scripts/keyword_check.py "<keyword>"` before planning or writing, and `python3 scripts/keyword_check.py` (whole site + plan) before publishing; both must pass. A tool's own pricing ('<tool> pricing') belongs to its review page; '<tool> alternatives' to its alternatives page; '<a> vs <b>' to the comparison; a category's head terms ('crm software', 'password manager') to its shortlist. Guides take informational or cost/how-to keywords around them ('what is X', 'X cost', 'how to Y').
One search intent per article; check the pillar and siblings don't already answer it.
Facts: prices/plans from category data in code; laws, deadlines and statistics only from official sources fetched the same day, listed in 'sources'.
Every article: link to its pillar in the first two paragraphs, and to 2+ sibling articles or comparisons; the build adds the pillar's Guides block.
No author names, no hands-on test claims, no invented examples presented as real customers.
